learningObjective: Reason about when inserting a layout-transform op in a graph is profitable and when it is not.

canonicalClaims.claim: Inserting a layout-transform op is a cost-benefit decision: it is profitable when the target-layout kernel's time savings exceed the transform's cost plus any restoration costs for downstream consumers.
conditions: The target hardware has a preferred layout with a kernel implementation available.
The compiler can estimate transform cost and downstream layout requirements.
nonImplications: Does not imply the same layout is preferred on all hardware or all shapes.
Does not imply a single layout transform is enough; some pipelines insert multiple to isolate a hot region.

misconceptions.claim: NCHW->NHWC is always a pure view (metadata only).
misconceptions.whyWrong: The stride pattern of channels-last differs from NCHW-contiguous in a way that requires reordering elements in memory.

misconceptions.claim: Channels-last is universally faster than NCHW.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Some kernels/shapes/architectures still favor NCHW; the choice is empirical and hardware-dependent.
Layout-aware kernel selection can amortize transform cost easily on large workloads.

misconceptions.claim: If a layout transform requires a copy, the compiler must abort.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Copies are a normal cost; the decision remains cost-benefit.

implementationFacts: PyTorch channels-last is stride-only on the logical NCHW shape but requires copy from NCHW-contiguous
cuDNN convolution kernels prefer channels-last on modern NVIDIA GPUs for many shapes
Compilers plan layout globally to avoid ping-ponging
performanceScenarios: Layout-planning passes evaluate transform cost against kernel gains; poor plans introduce redundant copies.
